correctness.rationale: With b a cyclic permutation and c collapsing exactly {0,1}→2, every rank drop uses effective c, and after any c state 1 is missing, forcing at least one b between successive effective c uses. Thus deficiency s costs at least 2s-1 letters and equality forces the unique word c(bc)^(s-1). Its holes follow a direct induction: {1,3,...,2s-1} until the final odd-parity step, when odd n additionally loses 0. The next b sends the surviving set into positions omitting 0 or 1, so the following c is ineffective; uniqueness of any would-be bound-attaining word implies λ_n(ceil(n/2)+1)>2ceil(n/2)+1 for n>=4. Independent exhaustive subset BFS on n=3,...,10 reproduced every early unique optimum and strict next threshold. Finite data are corroboration; the universal lower and upper bounds use the hole induction.
